items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign
items.excerpt: Microsoft researchers uncover a sophisticated campaign leveraging AI and end-to-end automation to scale device code phishing. Threat actors generate live authentication codes on demand, significantly increasing compromise success rates and maintaining persistent access. The report highlights technical indicators, AI-driven lure generation, and recommends enforcing strict OAuth consent policies and continuous identity monitoring.

items.title: OAuth Device Code Phishing: 37x Surge in Enterprise ATO
items.excerpt: The Cloud Security Alliance documents a dramatic 37-fold increase in enterprise account takeovers driven by OAuth device code phishing. Attackers exploit the legitimate device authorization flow to bypass multi-factor authentication, tricking users into entering codes on malicious sites. This research outlines mitigation strategies, including conditional access policies, user training, and monitoring for anomalous OAuth consent grants.

items.title: Device Code Phishing is an Evolution in Identity Takeover
items.excerpt: Device code phishing is rapidly expanding across the threat landscape, fueled by newly released criminal toolkits and phishing-as-a-service platforms. Attackers utilize automated techniques to generate convincing lures that manipulate corporate validation workflows. Security teams must prioritize identity-centric defenses, monitor for suspicious OAuth token issuance, and educate users on recognizing device code prompts.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Device Code Phishing Campaign Bypasses Password Theft ...
items.excerpt: ReversingLabs analysts detail an active campaign targeting Microsoft 365 environments by combining realistic business-themed emails with a polished phishing kit. Attackers abuse Microsoft’s Device Authorization Grant flow to execute near-invisible account takeovers without stealing passwords. Defenders should implement application consent restrictions, monitor for unusual sign-in patterns, and disable unnecessary OAuth flows.

items.title: Device Code Phishing Hits 340+ Microsoft 365 Orgs Across Five Countries ...
items.excerpt: A widespread device code phishing campaign has compromised over 340 Microsoft 365 organizations across five countries since February 2026. By abusing OAuth protocols, attackers achieve persistent token hijacking and seamless account takeover. The article provides actionable guidance for IT defenders, including tightening conditional access rules, auditing third-party app permissions, and deploying identity threat detection solutions.

items.title: Abuse of Cloud-Native Infrastructure in Modern Phishing Campaigns - CYFIRMA
items.excerpt: Threat actors increasingly leverage cloud-native services to host phishing infrastructure, evading traditional blocklists and detection mechanisms. This report details how attackers abuse serverless functions, object storage, and dynamic DNS to create resilient, ephemeral phishing campaigns. Defenders must shift from static URL filtering to behavioral analysis and cloud workload protection to mitigate these evolving tactics.

items.title: Device Code Phishing Drives Identity Takeover Risks
items.excerpt: Corporate security leaders face escalating identity attacks that circumvent traditional multi-factor authentication. This analysis examines a device code phishing campaign that manipulates corporate validation workflows to seize high-value employee accounts. The report emphasizes the need for zero-trust identity architectures, real-time threat intelligence integration, and proactive user awareness programs to counter these sophisticated tactics.

items.excerpt:
Affected versions of Flowintel do not revoke existing authenticated sessions when a user’s password is changed.


This means that if an attacker already possesses a valid session—for example, from prior access or a stolen session token—the victim changing their password does not terminate that attacker’s access. The session remains usable until it expires naturally. The upstream commit describes this directly as:
